audioContext: Letter name: bāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot below. Compare ت and ث, which share its basic shape. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Mark name: fatḥa. The dotted circle is just a placeholder.
usage: A small stroke above the letter: بَ = ba. It adds a short vowel after the consonant, not a separate letter. The dotted circle shows where the mark sits; it is not an Arabic letter.

meaning: long ā; also a seat for hamza
audioContext: Letter name: alif (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Alif does not join the next letter. A plain ا usually extends an ā sound; أ and إ carry hamza and are taught separately. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: tāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Two dots above. Compare ب and ث. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: short i; sometimes e in Palestinian speech
audioContext: Mark name: kasra. The dotted circle is just a placeholder.
usage: A small stroke below the letter: بِ = bi. In this course a kasra can also help mark local e, including before a final ة. Follow the Latin reading for the exact vowel. The dotted circle shows where the mark sits; it is not an Arabic letter.

audioContext: Letter name: mīm (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: The head and tail change with position. Learn its connected forms as the same letter. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: nūn (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above. In connected text compare its dots and shape with ب ت ث ي. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Mark name: sukūn. The dotted circle is just a placeholder.
usage: A small circle above the letter: نْ in بِنْت (bint). It means no vowel after that consonant. It is often omitted in ordinary writing and at the end of a word. The dotted circle shows where the mark sits; it is not an Arabic letter.

meaning: short u; sometimes o in Palestinian speech
audioContext: Mark name: ḍamma. The dotted circle is just a placeholder.
usage: A small curl above the letter: بُ = bu. Local vowel quality varies; the Latin reading distinguishes u and o where useful. The dotted circle shows where the mark sits; it is not an Arabic letter.

meaning: y; also ī and often ē
audioContext: Letter name: yāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Two dots below. ي can be a consonant or part of a long vowel; compare final ى, which has no dots. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: w; also ū and often ō
audioContext: Letter name: wāw (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Does not join the following letter. و can be a consonant or part of a long vowel; the whole word’s reading decides. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Mark name: shadda. The dotted circle is just a placeholder.
usage: The small w-shaped mark doubles the consonant: دّ in بِدِّي (biddi). It can occur together with a vowel mark; it does not itself add a vowel. The dotted circle shows where the mark sits; it is not an Arabic letter.

audioContext: Letter name: hāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Ordinary h, different from ح. Its middle form looks different from its isolated form. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: shīn (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Three dots above. Compare س. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: word-final a or e; t in some combinations
audioContext: Letter name: tāʾ marbūṭa (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: This end-of-word form often has a or e in Palestinian speech, not a pronounced h. It is heard as t in combinations such as kāset mayy (a glass of water). It is not interchangeable with ه. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: th as in thin in formal Arabic
audioContext: Letter name: thāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Three dots above. In Palestinian words this may be t, s or th depending on the word and local variety; follow the word’s reading. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: j; often like the s in measure locally
audioContext: Letter name: jīm (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot below the bowl. Palestinian varieties differ between j and zh-like sounds; compare ح and خ. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: ḥāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: No dot. This throat sound is different from the ordinary ه h; compare ج and خ. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: khāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above the bowl. Compare ج and ح. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: dāl (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Does not join the following letter. It can still attach to a preceding letter. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: th as in this in formal Arabic
audioContext: Letter name: dhāl (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above. Does not join the following letter. Palestinian readings may use d, z or dh depending on the word and variety. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: rāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Does not join the following letter. Compare ز, which has a dot. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: zāy (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above. Does not join the following letter; compare ر. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: sīn (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: No dots. Look for the teeth in common print styles; compare ش. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: ṣād (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: A heavier, tongue-retracted s. It may affect neighboring vowels. Compare ض. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: ḍād (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above the ص-shaped body. Keep it distinct from ordinary د. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: ṭāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: No dot. A heavier, tongue-retracted t; compare ظ. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: ẓ: emphatic z in many local words
audioContext: Letter name: ẓāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above. Formal Arabic often has an emphatic dh sound; the Palestinian sound depends on the word and variety. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: ʿayn (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Not an a vowel and not hamza. The connected forms change substantially; use the shapes below. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: ghayn (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above the ع-shaped body. A voiced sound from the back of the mouth. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: fāʾ (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: One dot above. Compare ق, which has two dots in this script. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: q in formal Arabic; often ʾ locally
audioContext: Letter name: qāf (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Two dots above. This course usually reads ق as the glottal stop ʾ in urban Palestinian speech. Other local varieties use q, g or k; the letter stays ق. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: kāf (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Its small stroke in the isolated/final shape is part of the letter form. Compare the connected shapes below. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: lām (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: With alif it forms لا; that is a joined pair of letters, not an extra alphabet letter. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: ʾ: glottal stop, as in uh-oh
audioContext: Letter name: hamza (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: Hamza is a consonant and does not join on its own. It can also sit on ا و ي as أ إ ؤ ئ. It is not ع. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: alif maqṣūra (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: This final form is usually an ā vowel, not a y consonant. Compare ي, which has two dots. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: alif with hamza above (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: The small ء is hamza. This shape can carry a fatḥa or ḍamma, for example أَ or أُ. A glottal stop may be omitted from the beginning of the learner’s Latin reading. Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: ʾi at the start of many words
audioContext: Letter name: alif with hamza below (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: The hamza is below the alif. The kasra gives the short i, as in إِنْتَ (inta). Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

audioContext: Letter name: alif madda (not the sound of a syllable).
usage: The wave above alif indicates hamza plus a long ā. Compare آسِف (āsef, sorry). Read right to left. Letter dots belong to the letter; vowel marks are added separately.

meaning: an ending in a few common expressions
audioContext: Mark name: fatḥatān / tanwīn -an. The dotted circle is just a placeholder.
usage: Two strokes above: شُكْرًا (shukran, thank you). Useful in set expressions. This Palestinian course does not add formal Arabic grammatical case endings to everyday words. The dotted circle shows where the mark sits; it is not an Arabic letter.
